chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from the one who informed him, from Dorost, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:
Regarding the zakat, if a man sends it to a city other than his own city, he said: There is no problem if he were to send the third, or a quarter. The doubt is from Abu Ahmad.
ai.seo_question: Can a person send their zakat to a different city, and what portion should be sent?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the flexibility in zakat distribution, permitting the sender to remit either one-third or one-quarter of the total amount to a different city, reflecting the scholarly nuance regarding the exact proportion. The uncertainty attributed to the narrator Abu Ahmad highlights the transmission dynamics in Shia hadith literature, where slight variations in numerical rulings are preserved to indicate permissible alternatives rather than error. This ruling underscores the practical ease granted to individuals in fulfilling their zakat obligations across geographical boundaries.
